title: Cooperative victims end a 108-day protest after an eight-point agreement
summary: Victims of fraudulent savings cooperatives ended a 108-day protest in Kathmandu after reaching an eight-point agreement with the government, according to a 2025 Kathmandu Post editorial.

title: Supreme Court opens suo moto contempt case against the sidhakura.com website
summary: The Supreme Court began a suo moto contempt case against the publisher and editor of the website sidhakura.com for content defaming a justice. This case produced the later extended full bench verdict on registration of online and social media platforms.

title: Cooperative victims hold a relay hunger strike in Kathmandu and Chitwan
summary: Victims of cooperative fraud protested in Kathmandu and Chitwan over deposits not returned, with a relay hunger strike, and said the protest would continue until an earlier agreement was implemented.

title: Cooperative victims resume protests (third phase)
summary: After the March agreement, cooperative victims resumed a third phase of protests in June, on the Maitighar-Baneshwar stretch where they had held earlier sit-ins.

title: Prachanda loses confidence vote in the House of Representatives
summary: Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' lost a vote of confidence after CPN-UML withdrew its support. Reporting gives 63 of 275 members in favour, 194 against and one abstention. Oli, with Nepali Congress support, was set to be nominated as the next prime minister.

title: President Paudel appoints Oli as prime minister
summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel appointed CPN-UML chairman KP Sharma Oli as prime minister, after Oli staked his claim with the backing of Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba.

title: Oli sworn in for a fourth time and forms a 22-member cabinet
summary: KP Sharma Oli was sworn in as prime minister for the fourth time and formed a 22-member cabinet with two deputy prime ministers (Prakash Man Singh of Nepali Congress and Bishnu Prasad Paudel of CPN-UML). President Paudel administered the oath to 19 newly appointed ministers.

title: Oli wins a vote of confidence with 188 votes
summary: Oli won the vote of confidence required within 30 days of appointment: 188 of 263 lawmakers present voted in favour, 74 against, one abstained. Oli read out the seven-point Nepali Congress-CPN-UML agreement, which provides for Oli to lead for two years and Sher Bahadur Deuba to lead until the December 2027 general elections.

title: Cabinet decides to lift the TikTok ban
summary: At its regular Thursday cabinet meeting the government decided to lift the ban on TikTok that the Dahal government had imposed in November 2023. Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung announced the decision.

title: NTA orders internet providers to lift the TikTok block
summary: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority ordered internet and mobile service providers to remove the restriction on TikTok, formally ending the ban after the 22 Aug cabinet decision.

title: Parliamentary committee report finds Lamichhane complicit in cooperative fund misuse
summary: A parliamentary special committee concluded that evidence did not show Rabi Lamichhane to be innocent: funds from cooperatives were funnelled into Gorkha Media Network, where he had been managing director, using cheques he signed.

title: Nationwide floods and landslides, 26-28 September 2024
summary: Heavy late-monsoon rain from 26 to 28 September caused floods and landslides across Nepal, with the worst damage in the Kathmandu Valley. Death tolls differ by source and date (217, 219, 224, 249). The Oli government was criticised for a slow response and weak preparedness.

title: Supreme Court extended bench rules that online and social media platforms must register
summary: An extended full bench of the Supreme Court, convicting the sidhakura.com publisher and editor of contempt, ruled that domestic or foreign online and social media platforms should be mandatorily registered with the competent authority before operation and that mechanisms should monitor undesirable content.

title: Rabi Lamichhane arrested on cooperative fraud and organised crime charges
summary: A Central Investigation Bureau team arrested Rabi Lamichhane, a former deputy prime minister, from the Rastriya Swatantra Party's central office in Banasthali, Kathmandu, on charges of cooperative fraud and organised crime. He was taken to Pokhara.

title: Lamichhane supporters protest in Kathmandu and Pokhara; police use tear gas
summary: Police fired tear gas and used water cannon on thousands of supporters of Rabi Lamichhane near the district court. Protesters chanted against Prime Minister Oli and said the charges were politically motivated.

title: Cooperative victims protest at Maitighar
summary: Cooperative victims staged a protest at Maitighar, Kathmandu, demanding the return of their savings, which they say were embezzled.

title: Social Media Bill introduced in the National Assembly
summary: The government introduced the Bill on the Operation, Use and Regulation of Social Media in the National Assembly. Reporting disagrees on the day: Monday 27 Jan (Himalayan Times, 'on Monday'), 29 Jan (Nepal Economic Forum), 9 Feb (CPJ and Kantipur).

title: Journalists' groups and press-freedom bodies criticise the Social Media Bill
summary: The Federation of Nepali Journalists, other journalists' bodies and legal experts criticised the bill as a threat to freedom of expression; on 14 Feb the Committee to Protect Journalists urged lawmakers to reject it. The bill provides fines, licence revocation and prison terms of up to five years for users, and bars anonymous profiles.

title: Former king Gyanendra Shah appeals for public support on Democracy Day eve
summary: In a message ahead of Democracy Day, former king Gyanendra Shah called on 'all countrymen' to support him 'for the prosperity and progress of the country'.

title: Pro-monarchy supporters rally at Tribhuvan Airport as Gyanendra returns
summary: Thousands of supporters, Al Jazeera estimating 10,000, gathered at the airport entrance as former king Gyanendra Shah arrived from western Nepal; the Rastriya Prajatantra Party and pro-monarchy groups took part. Riot police blocked demonstrators from the airport premises and passengers had to walk to the terminals.

title: Cabinet removes Kulman Ghising as head of the Nepal Electricity Authority
summary: The Cabinet removed Nepal Electricity Authority executive director Kulman Ghising after a standoff over recovering dues from industrialists and over a bilateral energy trade deal with India that he signed on 12 February.

title: Protesters attack media offices at Tinkune; Annapurna Post office set on fire
summary: Protesters set fire to the Annapurna Post office and pelted the Kantipur Television building with stones. Video journalist Suresh Rajak, filming for Avenues Television from the roof of the Annapurna Media Network building, was killed in the fire.

title: Curfew imposed in Tinkune, Baneshwar and Koteshwor
summary: The district administration imposed a curfew from 4:25 pm in the Tinkune, Koteshwor, Sinamangal and Baneshwar area. The Kathmandu Post gives 4:25 pm to 10 pm on Friday, later extended until 7 am on Saturday.

title: Pro-monarchy protest turns violent at Tinkune; two killed
summary: A pro-monarchy demonstration at Tinkune, Kathmandu, led by businessman Durga Prasai and drawing 'hardly 5,000' people according to the Kathmandu Post, turned violent. Protesters threw stones, set fire to buildings and vehicles; police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets. Two people died and 45 were reported injured by the Kathmandu Post; other outlets give different injury figures. Curfew and an army deployment followed.

title: Court orders pretrial detention of Rabi Lamichhane; he is taken into custody
summary: A court ordered pretrial detention of Rabi Lamichhane in the cooperative fraud case and he was taken into custody from his home.

title: RPP demonstration for the monarchy and the release of arrested leaders (planned)
summary: The Rastriya Prajatantra Party planned a demonstration demanding reinstatement of the monarchy and release of party leaders in custody, with over 2,000 police to be deployed.

title: Durga Prasai arrested in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, over the Tinkune violence
summary: Police arrested Durga Prasai in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, and brought him to Kathmandu on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime. The Kathmandu District Court remanded him and an associate to 12 days in custody the same day. The two outlets name the associate differently.

title: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigns
summary: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigned on a Monday. The Kathmandu Post reports differences with Prime Minister Oli and Finance Minister Paudel, over teachers' demands, as the reason; the stated reason was health.

title: Nepal orders Telegram blocked
summary: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority instructed service providers to block Telegram on 18 July 2025. Nepal gave online fraud and money laundering as the reason (Access Now).

title: Kathmandu Post reports full text of the Supreme Court registration verdict
summary: The Kathmandu Post reported the full text of the Supreme Court verdict requiring registration of online and social media platforms, eleven days before the ministry's seven-day registration notice.

title: Ministry issues seven-day registration notice to platforms
summary: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology published a notice giving platforms seven days to register, naming Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, X and LinkedIn. It followed a Cabinet instruction of 25 August and a 2023 directive that requires platforms to register and set up a local presence.

title: 'Nepo kid' trend spreads on Nepali social media
summary: Nepali users began exposing the lifestyles of politicians' children and accusing them of misusing public funds, in a trend that came from Indonesia and the Philippines. Sources disagree on whether it began before or after the ban announcement of 28 August.

title: Early Nepal-focused "nepo baby" video posted on TikTok
summary: Onlinekhabar says one of the earliest nepo baby videos about Nepali politicians’ children was posted on TikTok on 2 September 2025 and drew over 350,000 views. The account holder is not identified. Three more videos followed on 6 September. The trend had come from Indonesia and the Philippines.

title: Registration deadline expires with no major global platform registered
summary: The seven-day window expired with none of Meta, Alphabet, X, Reddit or LinkedIn having applied. Five platforms (TikTok, Viber and three others, named differently across outlets) were listed; Telegram and one more were awaiting approval. The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera put the deadline on Wednesday 3 September; The Himalayan Times says it expired Thursday at midnight.

title: Ministry directs NTA to block unregistered platforms
summary: On Thursday 4 September 2025 a meeting at the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, chaired by Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung and attended by the NTA, telecom operators and ISPs, decided to block platforms that had not registered. Spokesperson Gajendra Kumar Thakur said unregistered platforms would be deactivated from that day and any platform completing registration would be reopened the same day. The government framed the move as enforcing a Supreme Court directive and curbing hate, rumours and cybercrime.

title: Political and rights-group reactions to the block
summary: Critics included CPN (Maoist Centre) chief whip Hit Raj Pandey, Nepali Congress general secretary Gagan Thapa (4 September), Digital Rights Nepal, CPJ, Amnesty International and, on 8 September, the UN human rights office. The Nepali Congress was divided: its Central Working Committee had opposed the closure, party president Sher Bahadur Deuba said on 6 September the government only wanted registration, and on 8 September Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma urged him to press for reopening.

title: Government orders 26 social media platforms blocked
summary: Nepal shut down access to platforms that had not heeded the 25 August Cabinet directive to register within seven days (CPJ). HRW describes a 4 September directive banning 26 platforms including Facebook, WhatsApp, X and YouTube.

title: Gen Z march called for 8 September
summary: From 6 September 2025 TikTok, Reddit and Discord filled with videos and posters announcing a protest on 8 September; AI-generated posters gave "Parliament Building" as the place. Hami Nepal’s founder announced the protest on Saturday, per India Today, while Onlinekhabar found no identifiable central organiser and Discord users picked Monday over Saturday. Maitighar was promoted as the gathering point because Parliament at New Baneshwar was a prohibited area. Demands: reopen social media, end corruption and nepotism. Organisers said it would be peaceful and non-political.

title: Discord server "Youths Against Corruption" opens
summary: At 9:35 pm on 7 September 2025 the first message appeared on a new Discord server called Youths Against Corruption, set up after Shaswot Lamichhane messaged Hami Nepal that morning. Within hours it carried protest guidelines (wear school uniform, document everything), a duty list, a protest website and banners with QR codes. Hami Nepal posted at 11:48 pm that it was not there to lead. A second server, Yuva Hub, was active from 7 September and Hami Nepal was admin of the first (commission report via Onlinekhabar).

title: Journalists protest the social media ban in Kathmandu
summary: On Sunday 7 September 2025 dozens of journalists gathered in Kathmandu with signs such as "no shutdown of social networks" and "freedom of expression is our right".

title: Security forces prepare for Gen Z protest
summary: On 7 September 2025 police deployed 3,441 personnel in Kathmandu Valley, then 505 more, with a command post under the chief district officer. Kathmandu Police spokesperson Apilraj Bohora said forces were on high alert after receiving videos calling for a peaceful protest but showing Parliament and Singha Durbar burning, and that violators would face action. Estimates of expected turnout differed widely between agencies.

title: AI-generated videos of Parliament burning circulate before the protest
summary: Before the protest of 8 September 2025, pseudonymous accounts posted AI-generated images and videos showing Parliament and Singha Durbar burning, gunfire and tear gas. A commission report cited by Kantipur and Onlinekhabar's retrospective both describe this. Cyabra's analysis, as reported by Onlinekhabar, says AI-generated images built momentum before the real protest.

title: First police barricades breached; water cannon and tear gas used
summary: Per Harvard's Atrocity Prevention Lab timeline, demonstrators breached the first police barricades by 11:38 am, security forces deployed water cannon, and tear gas followed at 11:55 am. Human Rights Watch says police used tear gas, water cannon and batons as marchers pressed against barricades.

title: Government announces the social media ban is lifted
summary: After an emergency cabinet meeting, Communication Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung was quoted as saying the government had withdrawn the ban. Al Jazeera says this was late on Monday night; AFP datelines it as Tuesday, a day after the deaths, and found major apps working in Kathmandu.

title: Cabinet meeting at the prime minister's residence, Baluwatar
summary: An emergency cabinet meeting took place on Monday evening at Baluwatar. Lekhak resigned during it, a probe committee was decided, and a later late-night meeting decided to lift the social media ban.

title: Congress and opposition leaders hold Oli responsible
summary: On the night of 8 September, Nepali Congress general secretary Gagan Thapa said the prime minister must take responsibility and called for the party to leave the government; senior Congress leaders including Shekhar Koirala made similar calls and the CPN (Maoist Centre) demanded Oli's resignation.

title: Gen Z protest clash in Pokhara
summary: Protesters gathered in the area of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers office and vandalised a government vehicle, after which police used tear gas and batons. INSEC reports 30 injured, five by police gunfire. The Kaski district administration imposed an indefinite prohibitory order from 2 pm.

title: Gen Z protest in Damak
summary: ANI reports that in Damak (Jhapa) protesters attempted to break municipal gates and set fire to several motorcycles, and that police responded with water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets.

title: Gen Z protests in Butwal and Bhairahawa
summary: Protests escalated in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area and the Rupandehi district administration imposed a curfew from 4 pm to 10 pm.

title: Gen Z protests in Biratnagar, Chitwan and other cities
summary: Kathmandu Post lists protests in Pokhara, Biratnagar, Janakpur, Hetauda and Nepalgunj; Himalayan Times lists Biratnagar, Butwal, Chitwan and Pokhara and reports curfews in Biratnagar (11 am to 10 pm), Birgunj (11 am to 6 pm) and Kavrepalanchok (from 12:15 pm).

title: Gen Z protests in Kathmandu and other cities, 8 September 2025
summary: Day-long protests against the social media ban and corruption. A rally began at Maitighar Mandala at about 9 am and moved to New Baneshwar, where it reached the Federal Parliament. Police and armed police used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and live fire; a curfew was imposed from 12:30 pm. Nineteen deaths were reported nationwide by night (17 in Kathmandu, 2 in Itahari) and between 340 and 400+ injured, with protests also in Pokhara, Itahari, Butwal, Bhairahawa, Damak, Biratnagar and Chitwan. The Home Minister resigned that evening and the cabinet lifted the social media ban late that night.

title: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak resigns
summary: Lekhak submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Oli during the cabinet meeting at Baluwatar on Monday evening, citing moral grounds, after pressure from Nepali Congress leaders.

title: Kathmandu hospitals receive dead and injured protesters
summary: Civil Service Hospital, the National Trauma Centre, Everest Hospital, Kathmandu Medical College and Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital received the dead and injured. HRW reports Civil Service Hospital treated 221 injured patients and the Trauma Centre received 8 dead or later dead. The per-hospital death split differs between outlets.

title: Journalist shot while reporting near Parliament
summary: Harvard's timeline records that a Naya Patrika journalist was shot while reporting at 1:20 pm. INSEC's report says police gunfire affected protesters and journalists.

title: Rally marches from Maitighar to New Baneshwar
summary: By mid-morning the rally moved toward New Baneshwar with songs and banners. Protesters tore down posters of the then prime minister near Bijuli Bazaar. By noon thousands occupied the traffic island at Baneshwar and gathered outside the Parliament building.

title: Parliament gate vandalised and set on fire
summary: Protesters vandalised the Parliament gate in New Baneshwar and, per Setopati, set the main gate on fire.

title: Police fire on protesters at Parliament and New Baneshwar
summary: Police and armed police used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and live ammunition. Firing came from inside the Parliament compound, including by the Special Task Force with INSAS and SLR rifles (Kathmandu Post). HRW documents lethal force between about 12:30 and 4 pm. The start time of the shooting is reported as 12:37 pm (Harvard), after a 12:40 pm radio order (BBC, via Ratopati), or just before 1 pm (Kathmandu Post). Seventeen died in Kathmandu hospitals by night.

title: Police fire on protesters in Itahari
summary: Protesters arrested youths involved in arson at the sub-metropolitan city office; demonstrators then marched to the Area Police Office and threw stones, and police opened fire, killing two men estimated at 25 and 30. The injured were taken to BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences in Dharan. A curfew followed in Itahari.

title: Police fire tear gas inside Civil Service Hospital compound
summary: Around 3 pm police entered the Civil Service Hospital premises in New Baneshwar and fired tear gas, per Harvard. HRW's 9 September statement also says tear gas was used at Civil Hospital, where some of the injured were taken.

title: Police order to use necessary force ('Peter 1')
summary: According to police radio logs reported by the BBC, a call sign 'Peter 1', identified as IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, told officers to use necessary force at 12:40, ten minutes after the curfew. The report says a second order followed at 12:41 from the operations in-charge. AFP adds that police said Khapung acted after authorisation from a government security committee headed by a senior civil servant.

title: Protesters climb Parliament gate and walls
summary: Around twenty people had climbed the main gate of the Federal Parliament by 12:08 pm, per Harvard; the Kathmandu Post says some youths climbed the walls to plant the national flag; Himalayan Times says protesters broke into restricted zones and entered the premises. HRW says police fired after people climbed on the wall outside Parliament.

title: Rally gathers at Maitighar Mandala
summary: Demonstrators, many in school or college uniform and calling themselves Gen Z, gathered at Maitighar in central Kathmandu from about 9 am. The Kathmandu Post photo story says the rally was organised by the Hami Nepal group with prior approval; leaders urged no vandalism, arson or violence.

title: Army chief addresses the nation
summary: Per The Tribune, Army chief Ashok Raj Sigdel addressed the nation around 9 pm on 9 September, urging calm.

title: Army denies reports that the President resigned
summary: The Week, citing AFP and ANI, reports the army said President Ram Chandra Paudel had not resigned after reports to that effect.

title: Army deployed as arson ends
summary: HRW says the arson continued until around 10 p.m. on 9 September, when the army was deployed. The commission report, as summarised by Ratopati, recommends action against military commanders for delayed mobilisation.

title: Army airlifts ministers from Bhaisepati quarters
summary: Nepali Army helicopters took ministers out of the ministers' quarters in Bhaisepati to a secure location. The quarters were later reported set on fire.

title: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)
summary: After PM Oli resigned on 9 September and the army took security command, Chief of the Army Staff Ashok Raj Sigdel opened talks with Gen Z representatives and other stakeholders at Army Headquarters. President Ram Chandra Paudel joined the process, which moved to Sheetal Niwas on 11 September and ended with the agreement of 12 September on Sushila Karki as interim prime minister and the dissolution of the House of Representatives.

title: Arson and attacks on state buildings, 9 September 2025
summary: Second day of unrest. Protesters set fire to the Federal Parliament, Singha Durbar, the Supreme Court and the presidential residence Shital Niwas, attacked the Kantipur complex and homes of political leaders, and prisons were attacked. HRW says arson continued until about 10 p.m., when the army was deployed.

title: Attacks on leaders' homes and party offices
summary: On 9 September protesters set fire to the residences of prominent politicians and entered the office of Nepal's largest party (Al Jazeera); Newschecker reports the house of communication minister Prithvi Subba Gurung in Lalitpur was targeted. Locations are neighbourhood level only.

title: Banepa police station arson
summary: Newschecker identifies a viral video as an arson attack on a police station in Banepa, Kavrepalanchok, on 9 September 2025.

title: Former President Bhandari's residence in Bhangal set on fire
summary: Protesters set fire to the Bhangal residence of former president Bidya Devi Bhandari. Setopati says she was taken to a safe location.

title: Bhat-Bhateni stores looted and burned
summary: Of 28 Bhat-Bhateni outlets, 21 were damaged on 9 September; 12 were looted, set on fire and reduced to ruins (including Naxal, Maharajgunj, Boudha, Koteshwor, Baluwatar warehouse, Pokhara, Chitwan, Hetauda, Birtamod, Damak, Biratnagar and Dharan) and nine were vandalised and stripped of goods.

title: Biratnagar provincial and district offices burned
summary: Ratopati reports protesters entered the Koshi Provincial Assembly building and fire broke out in its premises, and that the Biratnagar High Court, Morang District Court, the District Administration Office and the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers office were set on fire and vandalised.

title: Central Jail (Sundhara) break
summary: On the night of 9 September, inmates who had left Nakkhu reached the Central Prison in Sundhara, Kathmandu, and security personnel there surrendered within minutes, according to Republica. Republica counts 1,400 escaped; INSEC counts 3,003.

title: Chitwan and Kanchanpur offices burned
summary: The Kathmandu Post reports 79 government offices and at least 17 private homes and businesses were torched in Chitwan district, and police confirmed over 30 government offices, 17 political leaders' houses and four commercial buildings were attacked in Kanchanpur.

title: Chitwan district administration office attacked
summary: Newschecker places a viral video at the Chitwan district administration office on 9 September 2025, citing a Kathmandu Post report of attacks on public offices that day.

title: Curfew in Kathmandu Valley, defied by protesters
summary: Curfew orders covered Kathmandu Valley on 9 September. Tribune reports the Kathmandu District Administration Office announced a curfew from 08:30 until further notice. Protesters defied it. AFP reported soldiers enforcing the curfew by loudspeaker on the following day.

title: Dahal's house in Chitwan set on fire
summary: Onlinekhabar reports protesters set fire to the Chitwan house of Maoist Centre chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal.

title: Protesters attack Dahal's residence in Khumaltar
summary: Protesters gathered in Khumaltar on Tuesday morning and threw stones at the residence of Maoist Centre chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal and vandalised a police post there, according to Setopati. Other outlets say the residence was vandalised or set ablaze.

title: Deputy PM Prakash Man Singh's house in Thamel set on fire
summary: Onlinekhabar reports protesters set fire to the Chaksibari, Thamel house of Deputy Prime Minister and Urban Development Minister Prakash Man Singh and burned six vehicles. Singh and his family had been moved to safety beforehand.

title: Sher Bahadur Deuba and Arzu Rana Deuba attacked at home
summary: Protesters entered the Budhanilkantha residence of Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba, beat and dragged him and his wife, Foreign Minister Arzu Rana Deuba, and handed them to the army or security personnel. Video showed both injured. They were treated at the Nepali Army hospital and Himal Press reported them out of danger on 10 September.

title: Dhangadhi and Kailali offices burned
summary: The Kailali District Administration Office's preliminary report counted 108 government buildings torched, vandalised or looted and 600 vehicles. Offices burned in Dhangadhi included Nepal Telecom, the Electricity Authority, the Health Office, Seti Provincial Hospital and the District Administration Office.

title: Dillibazar Jail unrest
summary: Inmates at Dillibazar Jail in Kathmandu demonstrated and tried to leave under the watch of Nepali Army personnel. Republica gave two accounts: that inmates broke the army cordon and escaped, and that none managed to flee.

title: False reports of the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar spread in Indian media
summary: Indian outlets, and The Business Standard citing family sources, reported on 9 September 2025 that Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar, wife of former Prime Minister Jhalanath Khanal, had died after protesters set their home on fire. Fact-checkers and Khanal himself said on 11 and 12 September that she was alive and in critical condition. See claim:chitrakar-died-on-9-september.

title: Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel chased and beaten by protesters
summary: Video showed Finance Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel running on foot while protesters chased and hit him. Gulf News adds he was stripped and pushed into a river.

title: Communication Minister Gurung's house in Sunakothi set on fire
summary: Protesters set fire to and pelted stones at the house of Communication and IT Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung in Sunakothi, Lalitpur. Police superintendent Chakra Raj Joshi said it was under control.

title: Hetauda offices burned
summary: Ratopati reports Bagmati Province government office buildings in Hetauda burning from about 1 pm; INSEC Makwanpur lists the Province Police Office, District Court, Patan High Court Hetauda Bench, the NHRC office and several ministries damaged.

title: Hilton Kathmandu set on fire
summary: Daily Mirror reports that agitators set fire to the Hilton Hotel in Kathmandu on 9 September.

title: House of the Maoist Centre chairman's daughter set on fire in Dholahiti
summary: Setopati reports that a body was found on 10 September in a house in Dholahiti, Lalitpur, belonging to the Maoist Centre chairman's daughter, after the house was set ablaze during the protest. Police had not identified the dead man. The family member is not named here.

title: Hyatt Regency and other hotels attacked
summary: Reuters reports the Hyatt Regency near Boudhanath was damaged by protesters (manager Bhushan Rane reported no guest or staff injuries) and that lawmaker Rajendra Bajgain said the Varnabas Museum Hotel was targeted in an arson attack. Nepali Times lists the Chhaya Centre in Thamel as burning.

title: Indian TV channels broadcast foreign-hand theories about the protests
summary: On or before 9 September 2025 Indian news channels linked the protests to a foreign hand: Republic TV called it a CIA plot, Times Now Navbharat spoke of a China-America struggle, and Aaj Tak said Hami Nepal had received Rs 20 crore from Coca-Cola and Viber. Newslaundry criticised the coverage in a piece of 9 September.

title: Jhumka Jail (Sunsari) break
summary: INSEC reports 1,552 inmates escaped from Jhumka Jail in Sunsari; Republica reports over 1,500 in Sunsari.

title: Kailali jail break
summary: Onlinekhabar reported at 16:59 on 9 September that all inmates had left Kailali Prison after people who occupied the facility let them out; Republica counts over 600 escaped in Kailali.

title: Kantipur complex attacked
summary: HRW says 10 to 15 men with sticks, knives and gasoline vandalised the Kantipur Television headquarters between 1:30 and 2 p.m. on 9 September. Al Jazeera's live blog reports protesters setting fire to a building housing Kantipur Publications, in an entry stamped 12:50 GMT (18:35 Nepal time).

title: Kaski jail break
summary: Nearly all inmates of Kaski Jail escaped, according to INSEC (773 capacity, 27 remained); Republica counts nearly 800 inmates fled in Kaski.

title: Former PM Jhalanath Khanal's home in Dallu set on fire
summary: A mob set fire to the Dallu home of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal on Tuesday morning. His wife, Rajyalaxmi (Ravi Laxmi) Chitrakar, was inside and was severely burned. She was treated at the Army Hospital in Chhauni, then at Kirtipur burn hospital, then in Delhi.

title: Former Home Minister Lekhak's residence in Naikap torched
summary: Protesters torched the residence of Ramesh Lekhak, who had resigned as home minister the previous evening.

title: Janakpur and Madhesh Province offices burned
summary: INSEC reports damage in all eight Madhesh districts, including the Madhesh Provincial Assembly and Chief Minister's Office area in Janakpurdham, the Janakpurdham Sub-Metropolitan City office and the Jaleshwar jail.

title: CPN (Maoist Centre) central office set on fire
summary: Setopati reports protesters set fire to the Maoist Centre central office in Paris Danda, Kathmandu, on Tuesday afternoon.

title: Ministers resign from the Oli cabinet
summary: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak resigned on the evening of 8 September. On 9 September Agriculture Minister Ram Nath Adhikari, Youth and Sports Minister Tejulal Chaudhary, Health Minister Pradip Paudel (all Nepali Congress) and Water Supply Minister Pradip Yadav (Janata Samajwadi Party) followed.

title: Ministries and state offices burned in Kathmandu
summary: Reporting lists several federal offices burned or destroyed on 9 September, among them the Ministry of Health and Population on Ram Shah Path, the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministries of Home and Finance, the Attorney General's Office, the anti-corruption commission (CIAA) office in Tangal, and the Department of Roads and Department of Transport buildings.

title: Nakkhu Prison break
summary: Inmates left Nakkhu Prison in Lalitpur on 9 September. Republica reports more than 3,300 escaped and that escapees from Nakkhu went on to the Sundhara Central Prison; INSEC lists a Lalitpur jail figure of 1,280.

title: Arson and looting wave across Nepal, 9 September 2025
summary: On 9 September 2025, a day after police fire on protesters, crowds burned government buildings, party offices, police stations, media offices, hotels and shops in Kathmandu and in provincial and district centres. Reporting names Singha Durbar, the Supreme Court, the parliament complex, provincial assemblies, district offices and the Bhat-Bhateni stores among the targets.

title: Naubasta Regional Jail and juvenile home unrest
summary: PTI, citing The Rising Nepal, reports five juvenile inmates died in a clash with security personnel at the Naubasta Correctional Home in Banke on the night of 9 September, and that 149 of 585 prison inmates and 76 of 176 juvenile detainees escaped.

title: Nepali Congress leaders demand Oli resign and the party quit the government
summary: Gagan Thapa called for Oli to resign and for the party to leave the government. The general secretaries said the seven-point agreement with CPN-UML was no longer relevant and urged Deuba to recall all ministers.

title: Nepalgunj government offices burned
summary: INSEC reports protesters set fire to and vandalised government offices in Nepalgunj Sub-metropolitan City, including the District Administration Office, Land Revenue Office, District Court, Survey Office and Internal Revenue Office, and burned police posts at several intersections.

title: Nepali Congress central office in Sanepa set on fire
summary: Protesters broke the windows of the Nepali Congress central office in Sanepa with stones and set it on fire on Tuesday afternoon.

title: Old Pashupatinath Temple footage spreads as an attack by protesters
summary: From 9 September 2025 a video of a crowd at the gate of Pashupatinath Temple was shared and broadcast in India as protesters attacking the temple. AFP, Newschecker, BOOM and Alt News traced it to a festival procession in March 2025, and a monk told AFP that everything was peaceful inside the temple.

title: Oli, Dahal, Nepal and ministers moved to Shivapuri
summary: Setopati reports the army flew Oli from Baluwatar by helicopter immediately after his resignation, and that Dahal and Madhav Kumar Nepal were flown from Singha Durbar. All were kept at the Army Command and Staff College in Shivapuri. Oli later said he was at the Shivapuri barracks. Kantipur reports the army airlifted 61 people, including VIPs and family members.

title: Oli calls an all-party meeting
summary: Oli called an all-party meeting for six in the evening on Tuesday.

title: Oli's private residence in Balkot set on fire
summary: Protesters set fire to Prime Minister Oli's private residence in Balkot, Bhaktapur, on Tuesday. Setopati reports police fired tear gas but could not protect the house.

title: Oli resigns as prime minister
summary: KP Sharma Oli submitted his resignation to President Ram Chandra Paudel on Tuesday afternoon under Article 77(1)(a) of the Constitution. The Prime Minister's Secretariat confirmed it and the President accepted it the same afternoon. Himalayan Times pages are stamped 14:31 (resignation) and 15:03 (acceptance).

title: More than a dozen media outlets attacked
summary: RSF counted over a dozen media outlets and journalists' organisations attacked on 9 September, including Annapurna Post, Annapurna Media Network, Avenues Television, ABC Television, ITV Nepal, Radio Nepal and Nepal Television, ThahaKhabar.com and several regional radio stations and papers.

title: Federal Parliament building set on fire
summary: Protesters broke into the Parliament premises and set the main building on fire on 9 September; Reuters reports army firefighters fighting a blaze in the main hall the next day.

title: Party offices set on fire
summary: The Nepali Congress central office in Sanepa and the CPN-UML central office in Chyasal, both in Lalitpur, were vandalised and set on fire. INSEC reports further party offices burned in Surkhet, Jumla and Kalikot, and the Kailali administration counted eight or nine party offices and leaders' homes set on fire.

title: Prime Minister's residence at Baluwatar set on fire
summary: PTI reports protesters set fire to the Prime Minister's residence at Baluwatar. Setopati's Wednesday field report says the prime minister's residence in Baluwatar was completely destroyed. The Karki commission later recommended action against the army commander responsible for security at Baluwatar.

title: Pokhara government offices burned
summary: In Pokhara, protesters set fire to the Gandaki Provincial Assembly Secretariat, the Office of the Chief Minister, the District Administration Office (Kaski), the Provincial Policy and Planning Commission and other offices; Himalaya Press reports 172 government vehicles torched or vandalised in Gandaki.

title: Police stations and posts burned nationwide
summary: Republica reports about 218 police stations, circles, beats, divisions, bureaus and offices were vandalised and burned, largely on 9 September, with 112 completely destroyed and 96 damaged, and over 12,000 police uniforms burned. INSEC lists nine police offices damaged in Parsa district.

title: President Paudel appeals for restraint and dialogue
summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel said Oli's resignation had been accepted and appealed to all parties to remain restrained and come to the negotiating table.

title: President Paudel's private residence vandalised
summary: Protesters stormed the private residence of President Ram Chandra Paudel in Bohratar, throwing his portrait down the staircase. ANI reports parts of the property were reportedly set on fire; Business Today says it was set ablaze.

title: Prison breaks
summary: Prisons were attacked on 9 September. HRW says thousands of prisoners were freed; Fox News reports that two prisons in western Nepal were stormed with nearly 900 escapes; the commission report as summarised by Ratopati gives 14,555 inmates escaped from various prisons.

title: Rabi Lamichhane leaves Nakkhu Prison
summary: RSP chair Rabi Lamichhane, held at Nakkhu on a cooperative fraud case, left the prison on 9 September. Onlinekhabar reports he was handed to his wife after police said they could no longer provide security; Republica reports he left on a letter that was later called counterfeit, after supporters pressed the outnumbered guards.

title: RPP lawmakers resign
summary: Setopati reports 13 federal and 28 provincial lawmakers of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party resigned on Tuesday afternoon.

title: RSP lawmakers announce resignations
summary: Lawmakers of the Rastriya Swatantra Party began announcing resignations in quick succession on Tuesday. Setopati later put the number at twenty.

title: Army and security agencies call for dialogue
summary: The Nepali Army, other security agencies, the Chief Secretary and the Home Secretary issued a joint statement calling for a peaceful solution through political dialogue.

title: Security chiefs tell Oli they cannot guarantee citizens' safety
summary: Himal Press reports that Army chief Ashok Raj Sigdel, Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung and Armed Police Force head Raju Aryal briefed Oli that they could not guarantee citizens' safety if he stayed in office. Oli first said he would not resign.

title: Shital Niwas set on fire
summary: HRW says the presidential palace, Shital Niwas, was on fire by 4:25 p.m. on 9 September.

title: Singha Durbar set on fire
summary: Protesters entered Singha Durbar through its western gate on 9 September and set the main administrative complex ablaze.

title: Supreme Court building set on fire
summary: The Supreme Court building was torched on 9 September. HRW places it shortly after the attack on Kantipur Television; the court later worked from a tent on its premises.

title: Karnali Provincial Assembly set on fire in Surkhet
summary: Protesters set fire to the Karnali Provincial Assembly in Surkhet in the evening of 9 September, including the building with the Speaker's office; INSEC also lists the Surkhet city hall, Birendranagar Municipality Office and the Provincial Auditor General's Office as damaged.

title: Tribhuvan International Airport closed
summary: Tribhuvan International Airport stopped flights from 12:45 pm on 9 September; Onmanorama says many airline crew could not reach the airport. Air India and IndiGo cancelled Kathmandu flights. Protesters gathered at the airport gate and the Nepali Army was deployed there. The closure was extended on 10 September, first until noon and then until further notice, citing curfew, conditions in the Valley and smoke on the runway.

title: CPN-UML central office in Chyasal set on fire
summary: Protesters set fire to the CPN-UML central office in Chyasal, Lalitpur, on Tuesday afternoon.

title: Army chief tells foreign military attaches the army is not staging a coup
summary: Around 4 pm on 10 September, army officials invited military attaches of Kathmandu embassies to Army Headquarters; Sigdel told them it was not a military takeover. The Kathmandu Post also reports that a young negotiator asked Sigdel whether he was staging a coup that afternoon.

title: Army takes control of Kathmandu
summary: Armed soldiers took control of Kathmandu on 10 September, ordering residents indoors under an indefinite curfew; soldiers guarded Parliament while army firefighters worked on the main hall.

title: Gen Z Discord session names Karki for interim prime minister
summary: On the Youth Against Corruption Discord server, moderated by Hami Nepal and livestreamed on YouTube, thousands of Gen Z participants debated who should lead an interim government. Karki was chosen: Al Jazeera and Wikipedia give a five-name shortlist (Karki, Timalsina, Dhakal, Sampang, Pun) with Karki on 3,833 of 7,713 votes; The Tribune gives a different runner-up. Timing of the vote is reported inconsistently.

title: Gen Z groups and Mayor Sampang meet the army chief at Army Headquarters
summary: On 10 September, groups claiming to represent Gen Z, and Dharan Mayor Harka Sampang, went to Army Headquarters to talk to Chief of the Army Staff Sigdel. One group left after Sigdel asked them to sit with Durga Prasai and representatives of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Crowds outside chanted different names (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang) and soldiers told them to agree among themselves and return the next day.

title: Oli says in a letter that he is at the Shivapuri army camp
summary: On the night of 10 September, KP Sharma Oli addressed a letter to "Dear Gen Z kids" stating that he was at the Shivapuri barracks, denying reports that he had fled the country. Setopati reported that Oli, Pushpa Kamal Dahal, Madhav Kumar Nepal and several ministers had been kept at the army centre for their safety.

title: Army eases curfew and prohibitory orders in Kathmandu Valley
summary: On 11 September the army shortened the prohibitory order (10 am to 5 pm) and kept the curfew from 7 pm to 6 am, allowing essential services and ticketed air travellers to move. Euronews reported the curfew as briefly lifted on Thursday; Al Jazeera said the nationwide curfew first imposed on Tuesday night would stay in place until Friday.

title: Gen Z leaders hold a press conference backing Karki and demanding dissolution
summary: ANI reports that on Thursday 11 September leaders of the Gen Z protest endorsed Karki at a press conference, citing her integrity and independence. PTI reports Gen Z leaders saying at a press meet that parliament must be dissolved and the constitution amended. AFP quotes Sudan Gurung telling reporters on Thursday that their "first demand is the dissolution of parliament".

title: Night consultations with party leaders at Sheetal Niwas
summary: From Thursday night into Friday morning talks at Sheetal Niwas ended without resolution. President Paudel invited Maoist Centre chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal on Thursday evening and Congress leaders were contacted by phone around 11 pm. Parties signalled support for Karki but wanted parliament kept.

title: President, army chief and Gen Z representatives hold talks on the interim leader
summary: On Thursday 11 September, President Paudel and Chief of the Army Staff Sigdel were due to talk to Gen Z representatives under army coordination. Reports differ on what stalled the talks: who should lead the interim government (ETV Bharat) or the constitutional route and dissolution of parliament (Nepali Times). The venue moved from Army Headquarters to the President's Sheetal Niwas on Thursday.

title: Ramechhap District Prison clash
summary: Nepal Army personnel opened fire during a clash at Ramechhap District Prison when inmates tried to break out, demanding to go home. Reports give 12 or 13 injured. The number of inmates killed is two in Himalaya Press and the Himalayan Times and three in PTI.

title: House of Representatives dissolved and election set for 5 March 2026
summary: Parliament was dissolved with effect from 11 pm on 12 September under a notification of the President's Office, on the recommendation of the interim government approved at Karki's first cabinet meeting. President Paudel announced fresh elections for 5 March 2026. Nepali Congress, CPN-UML and Maoist Centre called the dissolution unconstitutional.

title: Sushila Karki sworn in as interim prime minister
summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel administered the oath to former Chief Justice Sushila Karki, 73, as interim prime minister on Friday night; she is Nepal's first woman prime minister. The presidential press adviser announced the swearing-in for 9 pm; B360 posted that she was appointed at 9:20 pm. Her oath was broadcast on state television.

title: Sushila Karki appointed interim prime minister
summary: Sushila Karki, a former chief justice, took charge of an interim government on 12 September 2025 (HRW, UN News).

title: Friday talks at Sheetal Niwas agree on Karki and dissolution
summary: On Friday 12 September, after a meeting postponed from 9 am, the President, army chief, Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut, Maoist Centre leaders, Gen Z representatives and constitutional experts reached agreement: Karki as interim prime minister and dissolution of the House of Representatives. Sudan Gurung reportedly insisted on dissolution first; the army chief reportedly warned an emergency might be declared if no government was in place by evening.

title: Curfew and prohibitory orders lifted in Kathmandu Valley
summary: On Saturday 13 September the Nepal Army lifted the curfew and restrictive orders in Kathmandu Valley and other parts of Nepal; shops and markets reopened and cleaning drives began, though sensitive areas stayed off-limits.

title: PM Karki visits injured protesters in hospitals
summary: On Saturday 13 September Karki visited Bir Hospital, the Trauma Centre and Civil Service Hospital at New Baneshwar to see young people injured in the protests.

title: Rabi Lamichhane returns to Nakkhu Prison
summary: Republica reports Lamichhane returned to Nakkhu on Saturday evening, 13 September, after the prison issued a notice requiring all absconding inmates to return or face further charges.

title: Sudan Gurung's group protests at the PM's residence over the cabinet
summary: On Sunday night 14 September, a group led by Sudan Gurung protested in front of the prime minister's residence in Baluwatar, saying the cabinet expansion was done without consulting them and demanding Karki's resignation. Gurung said of Om Prakash Aryal "he's making himself home minister from inside!".

title: Karki consults aides and Gen Z leaders on the cabinet
summary: On 13-14 September Karki started consultations with aides and Gen Z leaders to form a cabinet of under 15 ministers. Gen Z members also held consultations on Discord. Names circulating included Om Prakash Aryal, Kulman Ghising and doctors Bhagawan Koirala and Sanduk Ruit. Hami Nepal leaders reportedly refused to join the government.

title: Karki takes charge of the Prime Minister's Office at Singha Durbar
summary: Karki took charge of her office in the Singha Durbar complex on Sunday 14 September (scheduled for 11 am per ANI) and held a minute of silence for those killed. In a first address she said "We will not stay here more than six months in any situation".

title: First three ministers sworn in: Khanal, Ghising and Aryal
summary: On Monday 15 September President Paudel administered the oath to Rameshwor Khanal (finance), Kulman Ghising (energy, water resources and irrigation, plus infrastructure and transport and urban development) and Om Prakash Aryal (home affairs, plus law, justice and parliamentary affairs) at a ceremony in front of the ruins of Sheetal Niwas.

title: Oli leaves army protection
summary: KP Sharma Oli, who had stayed at the army staff college in Shivapuri since 9 September, left on Thursday 18 September; sources told Setopati that he had started living in a rented house in the Gundu area of Bhaktapur. A UML publicity chief said the party had no information on where he stayed.

title: Five more ministers named and inquiry commission formed
summary: On Sunday 21 September Karki recommended five ministers (Anil Kumar Sinha, Mahabir Pun, Madan Prasad Pariyar, Jagdish Kharel, Sangeeta Mishra) and the cabinet formed a judicial inquiry commission under Gauri Bahadur Karki. ANI reports four ministers sworn in on Monday 22 September.

title: More than 6,800 escaped prisoners still at large
summary: On 25 September 2025 officials said more than 6,800 people who escaped prisons and custody during the unrest remained at large; the director of the Department of Prison Management is quoted on the number rearrested. The numbers inside the one retrieved article are not consistent with each other (about 6,900 rearrested against about 7,300 recaptured).

title: Forensic report: live bullets killed protesters
summary: Reuters reported that at least 33 protesters were struck by live bullets from high-velocity firearms, per the Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine's forensic department; of 34 bodies with bullet wounds, only one had a rubber bullet wound.

title: Ten left parties merge into the Nepali Communist Party
summary: Ten left parties, including the CPN (Maoist Centre), merged into the Nepali Communist Party with Pushpa Kamal Dahal as coordinator and Madhav Kumar Nepal as co-coordinator. The Tribune ties the merger to the September uprising and the announced March elections. CPN-UML stayed out.

title: Gen Z activists and police clash at Simara Chowk, Bara
summary: Six Gen Z youths were injured in a clash after Gen Z activists protested at Simara Chowk in Bara. Police arrested three people, including two ward chairs elected from UML; three others remained at large. Gen Z leaders accused police of security lapses. A six-point verbal deal followed at the Armed Police Force Technical School in Pathahiya.

title: HRW report on unlawful use of force
summary: Human Rights Watch published an analysis of 50 verified videos and other evidence on the 8 and 9 September violence.

title: Gen Z groups demand interim PM Karki's resignation
summary: Onlinekhabar reports protesters chanting for Prime Minister Sushila Karki to resign outside Baluwatar, a riot-police charge on organisers, and a petition by 23 Gen Z groups to the President asking for her removal for sidelining the movement's core demands. It also reports an allegation of nepotism against her chief private secretary.

title: RSP and Bibeksheel Sajha announce merger
summary: The Rastriya Swatantra Party, led by Rabi Lamichhane, and the Bibeksheel Sajha Party, headed by Samiksha Baskota, announced their merger on 30 November 2025. The unified party keeps the RSP name and the bell symbol.

title: Amnesty report on unlawful killings
summary: Amnesty International published findings that security forces used unnecessary and excessive force, based on verified eyewitness accounts, photographic and video evidence and interviews.

title: Oli re-elected CPN-UML chair at 11th general convention
summary: KP Sharma Oli was re-elected CPN-UML chairman at the party's 11th general convention with 1,663 votes against Ishwar Pokhrel's 564. Polling began on Wednesday 17 December and ended early on Thursday 18 December.

title: Election Commission publishes final voters' roll
summary: The Election Commission published the final voters' roll with 18,903,689 eligible voters, 915,119 more than in 2022, and designated 10,967 polling stations for the 5 March 2026 election.

title: Ujyaalo Nepal Party splits from RSP
summary: The Ujyaalo Nepal Party, widely considered Kulman Ghising's creation, formally split from the RSP on Saturday 10 January 2026, 12 days after the two parties announced unity under a seven-point agreement on 29 December 2025. The Kathmandu Post gives disagreement over distribution of portfolios as the sole reason.

title: Nepali Congress special convention elects Gagan Thapa president
summary: A special general convention elected Gagan Thapa Nepali Congress president as the only candidate on 14 January 2026. The same day the Deuba-aligned committee suspended Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma for five years. The Election Commission recognised the Thapa-led party on 16 January; the Deuba camp said it would contest this.

title: Oli denies giving a firing order
summary: KP Sharma Oli said he had not given an order to fire, and that no force was used at the Maitighar demonstration.

title: BBC investigation published
summary: BBC investigation, reported 26 and 27 February 2026, says a police call sign 'Peter 1', identified as former IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, ordered use of necessary force; it draws on over 4,000 videos and photographs, police radio logs and security officials' reports.

title: House of Representatives election
summary: Election to the 275-member House of Representatives, the first since the September 2025 uprising, held on the date set on 12 September 2025. Turnout was about 60 per cent. The RSP won 125 of 165 direct seats and 57 proportional seats, 182 in total; Nepali Congress 38; CPN-UML 25. Balendra Shah beat Oli in Jhapa-5 by 49,614 votes. Interim counts and analyst estimates ran ahead of the final total (an estimate of 185-190 seats on 9 March; 119 direct seats at an interim count).

title: Karki commission submits report on 8-9 September events
summary: The three-member commission chaired by Gauri Bahadur Karki handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on Sunday 8 March 2026, after questioning about 200 people. Outlets give different lengths (1,000 pages; 8,000-10,000 pages). The report recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung under Sections 181 and 182, and departmental action against police, Armed Police and Army officers. After outlets published its content, Karki decided on about 25 March to release it formally.

title: Commission report on Bhadra 23 and 24 incidents
summary: Commission of inquiry report on the 8 and 9 September events, reported as under cabinet review on 9 March 2026. It analysed CCTV and audio-visual material, a criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung was recommended (Kantipur headline), and the report records party-cadre involvement in arson (Ratopati).

title: Balendra Shah sworn in as prime minister
summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel swore in Balendra Shah (35, RSP) as prime minister on Friday 27 March 2026. Fourteen ministers took the oath at the ceremony, with Sudan Gurung as home minister. Sushila Karki had left office the same week.

title: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested
summary: Nepal Police arrested Oli and Lekhak early on Saturday 28 March 2026 from their homes in Bhaktapur, after the new cabinet decided to implement the commission report, in a case of negligence leading to deaths on 8 September 2025. Outlets differ on whether the warrants were issued by a court or were urgent warrants awaiting validation, and on the Penal Code sections.

title: UML secretariat meeting debates Oli's leadership
summary: At a UML secretariat meeting reported on 24 May 2026, Yogesh Bhattarai said the party could not move forward under Oli and that he should resign (reported indirectly by Spotlight Nepal).

title: Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods
summary: Floods on the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers in August 2026. By 5 October 2026 the government had suspended search and rescue except in emergencies and was moving to reconstruction. Not linked in the sources to the September 2025 protests; recorded because it is the main current crisis in the dataset's final weeks.

title: First anniversary: Gen Z Martyrs' Day
summary: Nepal observed 8 September 2026 as Gen Z Martyrs' Day, a public holiday. A programme by the GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society in New Baneshwor was attended by the Home Minister, ministers and families. Hamro Patro says 76 people died and the government has declared 45 martyrs; embassies including Australia, Norway, the UK, the US and Japan posted messages. An injured protester told Africanews the injured still needed state support.

title: Parties issue contrasting statements on the anniversary
summary: On 8-9 September 2026 the RSP and Lamichhane stressed state repression and the spontaneity of the movement; Oli described the 9 September destruction as the result of a planned attempt; Pushpa Kamal Dahal said the two days should not be viewed the same way; Gagan Thapa sent a video tribute. IANS summarises that the RSP played down property destruction while opposition parties stressed it.

title: UML vice-chair and general secretary submit opposing reports on Oli
summary: Vice-chair Ram Bahadur Thapa's 39-page report defended Oli and said losing an election does not require the chair to resign. General Secretary Shankar Pokharel's 65-page report recommended Oli step down.

title: Nepali Congress 15th general convention
summary: Leaders of the Congress, RSP, Nepali Communist Party and UML spoke at the Congress general convention at Khula Manch (Tundikhel), pledging cooperation on democracy and the constitution. Gagan Thapa criticised the prime minister's absence from Parliament; Dahal and UML's Pokharel raised fears of authoritarianism. Thapa's interview of the same date places the start on 6 October and refers to a parallel convention by Sher Bahadur Deuba.
